description: Led by an AI Engineer & IEEE wildfire author (2nd place Space Apps), FIRMSync tackles the NASA MODIS-VIIRS fire challenge. We are building a calibrated 25-year satellite fire calendar & early warning platform using NASA FIRMS data. AI & backend are ready! We are looking for: Frontend/Web Devs (React/Mapbox), UI/UX Designers, and GIS/Storytellers to build an award-winning MVP. Let's aim for Global Nominee together!
summary:
Wildfires in the Mediterranean Tell Atlas of northern Algeria, especially the rugged Kabylie mountains, pose extreme threats to human lives, ancient olive groves, and vulnerable rural communities under ferocious Sirocco heatwaves. Yet for over two decades, disaster responders have lacked a consistent historical fire record because NASA’s MODIS (1km) and VIIRS (375m) satellites detect active fire hotspots at vastly different spatial resolutions, creating artificial 7-fold discrepancies.

FIRMSync solves this challenge by harmonizing 25 years (2000–2026) of continuous NASA active fire observations across 7 northern Algerian wilayas into standardized Suomi-NPP equivalent baselines. Rigorously validated via Leave-One-Year-Out Cross-Validation (cutting wMAPE prediction error from 72.6% to 33.6%), FIRMSync equips the Algerian Civil Protection with an interactive burning activity calendar, custom Area-of-Interest (AOI) bounding box slicing, daily Fire Radiative Energy (FRE) disaster drilldowns, and zero-backend client-side GIS exports. FIRMSync transforms two decades of raw satellite pixels into life-saving wildfire intelligence.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

FIRMSync is a production-grade, zero-backend web application that harmonizes over two decades (2000–2026) of NASA MODIS (1km) and VIIRS (375m) active fire satellite observations into a unified, continuous burning activity calendar. Because VIIRS pixels are ~7× smaller than MODIS pixels, raw satellite records exhibit an artificial 4× to 11× surge in detected fire hotspots across Mediterranean vegetation.

FIRMSync resolves this discontinuity using a seasonal quantile transfer function calibrated over a 14-year sensor overlap window (2012–2025). Built using Leave-One-Year-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV), it normalizes both Terra/Aqua MODIS and NOAA-20 VIIRS into consistent Suomi-NPP equivalent units. Users can:

- Explore a 25-year monthly climatology across 7 vulnerable Algerian wilayas (Béjaïa, Tizi Ouzou, Jijel, Skikda, Bouira, Boumerdès, Algiers).

- Draw interactive custom Area-of-Interest (AOI) bounding boxes over specific forest massifs (e.g., Akfadou Oak Forest, Djurdjura Ridge).

- Drill down into high-resolution daily event progression telemetry for historic firestorms (August 2021 Kabylie disaster and August 2026 event) displaying cumulative Fire Radiative Energy (FRE) curves.

- Export standardized tabular CSV data, RFC 7946 GeoJSON GIS layers, and printable tactical briefing sheets for civil defense officers.

2. What benefits does it have and what is its intended impact?

- Saving Lives and Forest Ecosystems: Northern Algeria's Mediterranean coastal belt (Tell Atlas) experiences extreme summer Sirocco heatwaves, creating catastrophic wildfire complexes in wildland-urban interfaces. FIRMSync allows the Algerian Directorate-General of Civil Protection (Protection Civile) and forest conservators to immediately identify whether current burning activity is statistically normal or represents an extreme critical anomaly.

- Scientific Continuity: Solves the November 2, 2026 decommission of the Suomi-NPP satellite by establishing a seamless bridging model for NOAA-20 and the next-generation NOAA-21 (JPSS-2) VIIRS constellation, ensuring continuous climate records through 2030+.

- Zero-Barrier Accessibility: 100% client-side compilation ensures that emergency personnel in remote field stations with degraded cellular connectivity can run the entire tool offline without waiting on remote server processing.

3. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

- Data Engineering & Science Pipeline: Python 3.11, Pandas, GeoPandas, NumPy, and Scikit-learn for LOOCV transfer ratio calculations and machine learning hazard forecasters.

- Frontend Architecture: React 18, Vite 6, Tailwind CSS, and Lucide Icons.

- Geospatial & Visualization: Leaflet.js with custom spherical geodesic calculations, SVG cartographic rendering, and Inferno colormap palettes.

- Security & Quality Hardening: Python automated audit suites (`07_audit_run.py`, `09_audit_features.py`, `10_security_audit.py`) guaranteeing RFC 4180 formula-injection neutralization (CWE-1236), strict Content Security Policies (CSP), and zero secrets exposure.

- Hosting & Open Science: Deployed on Netlify with automated CI/CD; open dataset hosted on Hugging Face Data Studio.

4. How is your project creative?

- Physically Grounded Harmonization: Unlike black-box neural networks that obscure satellite measurements, FIRMSync uses empirical seasonal quantile scaling that preserves the physical proportionality of Fire Radiative Power (MW) and Fire Radiative Energy (Joules).

- Hybrid Cartographic Architecture: Combines curated administrative regional wilaya polygons with real-time dynamic bounding-box slicing, providing the convenience of predefined baselines with the flexibility of custom GIS selections.

- Zero-Dependency GIS Bounding Box: Developed a pure Leaflet-native bounding box tool with spherical area approximation, avoiding heavy 600 KB external GIS libraries and keeping the application lightweight and secure.

5. What factors did your team consider?

- Operational Reality of Civil Protection: Fire commanders cannot wait for heavy GIS software to load. FIRMSync delivers sub-second load times and one-click printable briefing sheets formatted specifically for crisis triage.

- False-Positive Mitigation: Implemented rigorous static cell filtering to eliminate non-wildfire industrial and gas-flaring heat signatures, ensuring only genuine vegetative and agricultural burns are analyzed.

- Constellation Continuity: Anticipated the orbital mechanics of the NOAA-20/NOAA-21 50-minute afternoon overpass offset, designing a forward-compatible schema for future JPSS missions.
